questions.q: What is the first stage of the asset lifecycle?
questions.explain: You first define the need and security requirements before purchasing anything.

questions.q: Which item should be included in the requirements specification during acquisition?
options: Support duration and certified erasure capability
questions.explain: Security requirements (support, encryption, compliance, end-of-life) must be written before purchasing.

questions.q: Which information should an asset record contain? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: A password must never be stored in the inventory; the other items are essential for tracking.

questions.q: Match each stage to its primary action.

pairs.right: Purchase with requirements written into the specification
Assign an owner and register the asset

questions.explain: Each stage produces an artifact: formalized need, contract, inventory record, certificate of destruction.

questions.q: A disk leaves the company without being wiped. Which artifact is missing to prove proper disposal?
questions.explain: A certificate of destruction (or erasure report) is the required proof at end-of-life.

questions.q: A service is used by a team without the security team's knowledge. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.explain: Shadow IT escapes inventory and therefore misses patching, monitoring, and end-of-life controls.
